stem:
For a school science exhibition, Meera makes a pinhole camera using an empty shoe box. She makes a tiny hole on one side and fixes a tracing-paper screen on the opposite side. She points the hole towards a burning candle kept in a darkened room.
Which image of the candle flame does she see on the screen?

options.text: an upright image, the same way up as the flame
an upside-down image of the flame
a circular bright patch, the same shape as the hole
no image, because the hole is too small for light to pass through

teacher.key_rationale: Light from the top and bottom of the flame travels in straight lines through the tiny hole and crosses over, so the top of the flame appears at the bottom of the screen and vice versa, giving an inverted (upside-down) image. A is the trap for assuming images made by light must be upright like a mirror image; C is the trap of thinking the image takes the shape of the hole; D ignores that the pinhole is precisely what forms the image.
